revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Square Mirrors
revealWordProblem.text:
The side lengths of two square mirrors are shown. Mirror A has sides of 2½ feet and Mirror B has sides of 1¾ feet.
Question: About how many times greater is the area of Mirror A than the area of Mirror B?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two square mirrors side by side: Mirror A is 2 and one-half feet across and Mirror B is 1 and three-fourths feet across.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find each area first. Mirror A: 2½ × 2½ = 5/2 × 5/2 = 25/4 = 6¼ square feet. Mirror B: 1¾ × 1¾ = 7/4 × 7/4 = 49/16 = 3 1/16 square feet. Now divide to compare: 25/4 ÷ 49/16 = 25/4 × 16/49 = 400/196 ≈ 2.04. Mirror A's area is about 2.04 times as large as Mirror B's.

conceptIntro.heading: Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers
conceptIntro.intro: A fraction division does not always give a whole number. A fraction answer means part of one more group.
conceptIntro.introEs: Una división de fracciones no siempre da un número entero. Una respuesta fraccionaria significa parte de un grupo más.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Multiply by the reciprocal to divide fractions, and read a fraction part of the answer as part of one more group.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Multiplica por el recíproco para dividir fracciones, y lee la parte fraccionaria de la respuesta como parte de un grupo más.

iDo.title: Example · The answer is not whole
iDo.titleEs: Ejemplo · La respuesta no es entera
lines: Lena has 3/4 cup of flour. One batch of muffins needs 2/3 cup. How many batches can she make?
Write the division. Then Keep, Change, Flip: 3/4 ÷ 2/3 → 3/4 × 3/2
Multiply the tops. Multiply the bottoms: 3/4 × 3/2 = 9/8
Write the answer as a mixed number: 9/8 = 11/8
Say what 11/8 means for Lena: 1 batch + 1/8 of a batch
3/4 ÷ 2/3 = 11/8. Lena can make 1 full batch and 1/8 of another batch.
linesEs: Lena tiene 3/4 de taza de harina. Una tanda de panecillos necesita 2/3 de taza. ¿Cuántas tandas puede hacer?
Escribe la división. Luego mantén, cambia e invierte: 3/4 ÷ 2/3 → 3/4 × 3/2
Multiplica los numeradores. Multiplica los denominadores: 3/4 × 3/2 = 9/8
Escribe la respuesta como número mixto: 9/8 = 11/8
Di qué significa 11/8 para Lena: 1 tanda + 1/8 de una tanda
3/4 ÷ 2/3 = 11/8. Lena puede hacer 1 tanda completa y 1/8 de otra tanda.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Find 1/2 ÷ 1/4. Then explain why the answer is bigger than 1/2.
Why is the answer bigger than 1/2? (The answer counts 1/4 pieces. Each piece is smaller than 1/2, so 2 of them fit.)
linesEs: Halla 1/2 ÷ 1/4. Luego explica por qué la respuesta es mayor que 1/2.
Mantén, cambia e invierte. Luego multiplica. (1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2)
¿Por qué la respuesta es mayor que 1/2? (La respuesta cuenta piezas de 1/4. Cada pieza es menor que 1/2, así que caben 2.)

tryIt.modelExplanationEs: Solo puedes invertir una fracción. 1{1/4} es un entero más una fracción. Como {5/4}, su recíproco es {4/5}. Luego {15/4} × {4/5} = {60/20} = 3.

onLevel.stem: A recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar. You only have a 1/6-cup scoop. How many scoops do you need?
choiceFeedback: Only 2 scoops of 1/6 cup makes 2/6 = 1/3 cup — not enough sugar. Use Keep, Change, Flip on 2/3 ÷ 1/6 and simplify what you get.
Multiplying doesn't answer 'how many fit.' Divide the whole by the piece size.
The dividend (whole) goes first. The divisor (piece size) is second.
hints: The recipe total is 2/3 cup; one scoop holds 1/6 cup — you're counting scoops, not multiplying.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: The student changed ÷ to × but forgot to flip the divisor. Keep 2/3, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/2 to its reciprocal 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. The correct quotient is 4/3 (1 1/3), not 1/3.
hints: After you change ÷ to ×, you must also flip the second fraction (the divisor).
The divisor 1/2 should become its reciprocal 2/1 before you multiply: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.
onLevel.explanation: The step that changed ÷ to × left the divisor as 1/2 instead of flipping it, so the problem turned into multiplication of the original fractions. Keep, Change, Flip turns the divisor into 2/1, giving 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. That size makes sense, because 1/2 is smaller than 2/3, so more than one copy fits.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso que cambió ÷ por × dejó el divisor como 1/2 en vez de voltearlo, así que el problema se convirtió en una multiplicación de las fracciones originales. Conserva, Cambia, Voltea convierte el divisor en 2/1, lo que da 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. Ese tamaño tiene sentido, porque 1/2 es menor que 2/3, así que cabe más de una copia.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante cambió ÷ a × pero olvidó voltear el divisor. Mantén 2/3, cambia ÷ a ×, y voltea el divisor 1/2 a su recíproco 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. El cociente correcto es 4/3 (1 1/3), no 1/3.
hintsEs: Después de cambiar ÷ por ×, también debes voltear la segunda fracción (el divisor).
El divisor 1/2 debe convertirse en su recíproco 2/1 antes de multiplicar: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.

onLevel.title: Find the Division Error
onLevel.correctWork: The student forgot to flip. 2/5 × 4/3 (flip the divisor 3/4 to get 4/3). Then 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.
hints: In 'Keep, Change, Flip' — which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (3/4) should become its reciprocal (4/3). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
onLevel.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step swapped the operation but left the divisor as 3/4, so no fraction was actually flipped. The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3, so the problem is 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, not 3/10.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de Conserva, Cambia, Voltea cambió la operación pero dejó el divisor como 3/4, así que en realidad no se volteó ninguna fracción. El recíproco de 3/4 es 4/3, así que el problema es 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, no 3/10.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó voltear. 2/5 × 4/3 (voltea el divisor 3/4 para obtener 4/3). Entonces 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.

onLevel.prompt: Is 3/4 ÷ 1/2 the same as 1/2 ÷ 3/4? Solve both and explain why or why not. What does this tell you about the order in division?
onLevel.sentenceFrame: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = ___ and 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = ___. These are ___ because ___. This shows that division is ___.
onLevel.hint: Explain how dividing by smaller fractions produces larger quotients using a real scenario.
hints: Don't assume the two divisions match — solve each one on its own first.

onLevel.explanation: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 becomes 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, while 1/2 ÷ 3/4 becomes 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, so the two expressions are not equal. Swapping the dividend and the divisor flips the quotient to its reciprocal, which shows that division is not commutative — order matters.
onLevel.explanationEs: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 se convierte en 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, mientras que 1/2 ÷ 3/4 se convierte en 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, así que las dos expresiones no son iguales. Intercambiar el dividendo y el divisor convierte el cociente en su recíproco, lo que muestra que la división no es conmutativa: el orden importa.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5. Before you submit, check that the fraction you kept (the dividend) is still facing the same way it started.
